title: TDS on FD (194A)
shortAnswer: Check if TDS applies to your fixed deposit interest.
longAnswer: Section 194A requires banks and post offices to deduct TDS at 10% on interest paid on fixed deposits and recurring deposits if the interest exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year (₹1 lakh for senior citizens). The TDS on FD Calculator takes the interest amount and your age to show the TDS to be deducted and the net interest. If your total income is below the taxable limit, you can submit Form 15G (or 15H for senior citizens) to prevent the deduction. TDS is not the final tax—if your slab is higher than 10%, you pay the difference when filing; if lower, you claim a refund. Interest is taxed at slab on accrual, and the TDS is a credit against that liability. The calculator does not compute the final tax—use the FD tax calculator for that. Match the interest with Form 26AS/AIS before filing. The threshold is per bank, not per account.
